_comment: The pre-registration of agent_architecture.md §7's last reporting rule: budget
and hyperparameters are fixed before any test run, all method debugging happens
on train, and every arm is reported on test — never 'best of'. Committed before
the registered search and before any test rollout; its sha256 travels with every
run (harness/preregistration.py), so an edit after the fact moves the hash rather
than quietly redefining what was promised. Amendments are appended to
'amendments' with their reason, never applied by rewriting a value in place.

supersedes.what_it_produced: eval/measurements/20260825T174410Z.json — the P8c run, reported in findings.md § The measurement run (P8c)
why_a_second_one: §7's own repeat condition fired on that run and this is the repeat it asks for
(T134). Residual exclusion counts diverged between the arms on the split
carrying the primary estimand — 14 of 125 baseline against 25 of 125 optimized
on test_seen, driven by `upstream` (20 vs 34) and `text_to_sql_agent` (1 vs 9) —
which is the architecture's stated condition for repeating a run, so P8c's
comparison is recorded and not established.
A repeat under registration 1 is not what is run here. The task model has moved
and so has the capture surface, both for reasons stated below, so this is a
fresh registration rather than a second run under the old one: nothing in it is
chosen to make a P8c number look different, and the two runs are reported side
by side as two measurements rather than pooled.

registered_against.note: T134's setup. The last commit before any rollout of this registration exists; it carries the capture widening, the model re-pin and the two thought-part fixes, and no test rollout has run against it.
registered_against.case_files_note: Byte-identical to registration 1's. The suite is not re-drawn for the repeat — a repeat over different cases would answer a different question — and `just cases-check` confirms the committed files are a fresh generation pass.

why_this_model: A DATED snapshot, which is the first time §5's model pin names something the
provider cannot silently replace. decisions.md § Model pinning records the
whole canary mechanism as a workaround for undated aliases; -0731 is not one,
so the canary becomes a second check rather than the only one.
It is also cheap enough to buy back the replication amendment 1 sold. At
$0.06/$0.12 per Mtok against gemma-4-31b-it's $0.10/$0.34, three repeats of
both arms on all three splits cost less than P8c's single repeat did.
one_model_in_both_roles: REGISTERED DEVIATION from §5, and the largest thing about this run that is not
a repeat. §5 asks for a reflection model distinct from the model under test so
that a result can be attributed to one of the two; here they are the same served
model on the same endpoint, so the search is a model reflecting on its own
rollouts and this run cannot separate 'the proposer is weak' from 'the task
It is chosen rather than inherited. P8c split the two roles across providers to
solve a quota problem (T128) that OpenRouter does not have, and holding the
teacher fixed while the student moved would confound the model change with the
role split. One model in both roles is the cleaner comparison against P8c and
the weaker claim about attribution; the pins stay two separate slots, so the
choice is recorded rather than lost.

basis: P8c's own token counts at this model's published rates: the registered search
spent 13.28M prompt and 0.109M completion tokens over 567 rollouts, and one
repeat of the measurement spent 13.90M and 0.112M over 562. Three repeats is
The estimate is a floor, not a ceiling. A reasoning model bills its trace as
completion tokens and P8c's task model emitted none, so completion cost may
run several times the number above — which is still cents against this limit,
and is why the limit is 6.0 rather than the estimate.

budget.if_exhausted: The split order below decides what is lost, exactly as amendment 3 of registration 1 decided it. Registered before any test rollout and on no test number.

baseline: The handwritten seed candidate at the pinned candidate_prompt_versions — the
evaluation root instruction plus the six tool texts, registered once and read
twice (T125), so the reference arm and the search's seed cannot drift apart.
It enters at 0.50 abstention accuracy by choice: T107 found T17a failing 3/3
on the handwritten instruction with correct reasoning and a wrong contract
encoding, and left it for the search, because the encoding lives in the
optimizable text. A candidate repairing it is measuring what the thesis claims
to measure, and this sentence exists so that improvement cannot later be read
as a baseline that was quietly weakened.
It is NOT P8c's baseline text. T136 added one sentence to each of the six tool
texts saying that the text is a tool declaration and naming the callable it
declares — 605 characters over six components, reaching the task model on every
rollout of BOTH arms. So it moves the reference arm and the search's seed by the
same amount, and a baseline number from this run is not comparable with P8c's.
optimized: Whatever candidate the one registered search selects. Not the best of several
searches, not the best iteration by test score, not a hand-picked candidate:
the search's own selection, on the aggregated scalar, over train alone.

measurement.pairing: the identical committed cases, in file order, for every arm and every repeat
repeats_note: Three, which is what registration 1 registered before amendment 1 cut it to one
on budget. The three repeats ARE the replication and are what makes the LLM
response cache's being off matter: a prompt-keyed hit would hand the first
repeat's bytes to the other two.

why: Registered rather than tuned quietly, because it changes the exclusion rate and
the exclusion rate is what §7 reads the arms against. The response cache is
keyed on the request, so a candidate reading 'the next d days' differently from
the oracle misses, and on the measurement path a miss excludes the case. ±1 was
sized on one behaviour the pilot observed; P8c then lost 30 of 56 test_unseen
cases in one arm and 28 in the other to those misses, and T22 and T23 were
measured in NEITHER arm — the holdout's population, not a rounding error.
±3 is a wider warm cache and nothing else: the neighbours are answered through
each family's own oracle, so no window here is one this repository computed.
509 → 947 entries, every case still reproduces its committed answer against the
live services, and `just capture-verify` replays all of them with zero live
calls.
what_it_does_not_fix: A miss is still possible and still excludes. What a candidate reaches for is
unknowable before the search, and this is a wider guess rather than a solution,
so §7 still publishes the exclusion count per arm and still reads each arm's
against the other's rather than against zero.

analysis.repeat_reduction: mean over the repeats per case, before any aggregation over cases
analysis.primary_estimand: the paired difference optimized - baseline, per metric, on test_seen
analysis.test_unseen_trajectory: per-template win/loss table; no accuracy and no interval
analysis.abstention: accuracy over the unanswerable cases and the false-abstention rate over the answerable ones, reported separately and never blended
analysis.exclusion: harness_error cases leave every aggregate and are counted per arm with their sources broken out; invalid_argument never excludes
analysis.parse_failure: reported apart from answer accuracy, so a candidate degrading the output format stays distinguishable from one degrading reasoning
analysis.residual_nondeterminism: MEASURED, from the three repeats per condition. This is the quantity registration 1 gave up under its amendment 1 and reported as unmeasured; every arm difference in this run is read against it, and a difference smaller than it is reported as within the noise floor rather than as a small effect.
analysis.multiplicity: no correction across the four metrics. They are four declared quantities, not a family searched over for a winner; the interval and the noise floor carry the uncertainty and the suite is stated to detect large effects only
comparison_with_p8c: REPORTED SIDE BY SIDE, NEVER POOLED AND NEVER DIFFERENCED. Three things moved
between the two runs — the task model, the six tool texts (T136) and the capture
neighbourhood — so a difference between the runs is not attributable to any one
of them. What carries across is the QUALITATIVE question §7's repeat condition
asks: whether the exclusion counts diverge between the arms again, and whether
the direction of the answer metric's movement reproduces. Both are stated as
such and neither is given an interval.

method_debugging: train only. Every defect the pilot and the packets found was found on train
or on the pilot's own cases. The two test splits have been run ONCE, under
registration 1, and their numbers are in findings.md — so unlike registration 1
this registration is not written by someone who has never seen a test number.
Nothing in it is chosen on one: the model was chosen on price and on being a
dated snapshot, the repeats restore what was registered before amendment 1 cut
them, the capture widening is driven by an exclusion count that §7 publishes
precisely so it can be acted on, and the split order is copied unchanged.
reporting: Both arms on all three splits, whatever the numbers are. A repeated run is
reported as a repeat, and §7's own repeat condition is the only one that
licenses it: residual failure counts diverging between arms mean the arms
were not measured under the same conditions. Diverging newly-recorded cache
entry counts are reported and never repaired.
stopping: The measurement is complete when both arms have three repeats on all three
splits. It is not stopped early on a favourable interval, and it is not

known_gaps.what: The reflective dataset reaches GEPA without its span half: MLflow stands down from tracing when ADK is already tracing, so the search reflects on `Feedback.rationale` and the inputs, and not on the ADK tool spans.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED in this run. tasks.md orders it before a rerun and it is not landed; the run proceeds with it declared rather than waiting.
known_gaps.effect: The proposer sees less about a rollout than the design intends, which weakens the search in both runs equally — P8c had the same gap — so it does not confound the comparison, and it does bound what a null result would mean.

known_gaps.what: The proposer is asked to rewrite, not to revise, and nothing checks a candidate that names a callable no toolset resolves. P8c's winner is what that produces: one tool description rewritten into a root-agent system prompt naming `agent_tool_predict_green_roof_water_balance_tool`, which does not exist.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED in this run. tasks.md orders it before a rerun and it is not landed.
known_gaps.effect: A candidate of this run may be broken the same way, and nothing will refuse it. T136's sentence inside each tool text is the seed-side half that IS landed, so the seed says what each text is even though the metaprompt does not constrain how much of it to change. Any candidate naming a callable outside TOOL_NAMES is reported in findings.md by hand for this run.

what: models.served_by: null → 'deepinfra'. Every OpenRouter call of this run is
pinned to one provider with allow_fallbacks=false, on all three paths: the
ADK rollout, the text-to-SQL chain's bare litellm calls, and GEPA's
budget.estimate.total: 3.35 → 4.4. The registered limit of 6.0 is UNCHANGED.
why: An endpoint is not a server, and this run had not noticed. OpenRouter serves
deepseek-v4-flash-0731 from 29 providers at quantizations from fp4 through
fp8 to bf16, and routes per request: the first smoke search drew five
different ones in eight calls. That is §5's provider-swap hazard occurring
INSIDE a single run rather than between two, where no canary taken before
the run can see it and where `endpoint` does not distinguish it. Nothing was
registered about it because nothing in the testbed had ever named it — the
text-to-SQL experiments solved the same problem first
(`experiments.text2sql.harness`, LLM_OPENROUTER_PROVIDER) and the testbed
did not inherit it.
The choice of provider is not arbitrary and is not cost-driven. Screened on
three failure modes: `relace` — the CHEAPEST, therefore the router's
preference, and priced at exactly what this registration originally
assumed — returns the chain of thought inside `content`, which is where the
SQL builder reads its query, and produced an 883-character 'SQL' beginning
'We need to query outflow table' in the smoke search; it also hung four
consecutive calls on a serial probe. `parasail`, `baseten` and `fireworks`
rate-limit. `open-inference` and `morph` answer cleanly at 40 s and 55 s
mean, which is nine to twelve times `deepinfra` and turns this run into
days. `deepinfra` answered 3/3, leaked nothing, honoured tool calls and
averaged 4.4 s.
No test rollout has run. The measured surface here is a provider screen on
throwaway prompts, not a split.
cost: About $1.05 more than the unpinned estimate, because the router's cheapest
provider is the one that cannot be used. That is the price of knowing which
machine answered, and it is paid inside the registered limit.
A hard pin fails loudly when deepinfra is unavailable rather than drifting
to another provider. A run that dies mid-measurement is the accepted
failure; a run that quietly finishes on three different servers is not, and
T135's per-condition write is what makes the first one survivable.
The comparison with P8c loses one more axis. P8c was unpinned, so its
numbers come from whatever mixture OpenRouter chose that day — which is
not recoverable after the fact and is now a fourth thing that differs
not_amended: The arms, the splits, the repeats, the pairing, the bootstrap unit and its
seed, the two gaps, the win/loss table, the exclusion rule, the diagnostics,
the capture neighbourhood, the budget LIMIT, and the whole protocol section.
The served model id is unchanged: this names which server answers for it.
